abstract: A rational Diophantine septuple is a set of seven nonzero rationals with 1 + xy a square for every pair; none is known. We study the same condition for members of the form x = ir, r rational: then 1 + xy = 1 - rr', and the condition becomes 1 - rr' = +-square, a mixed D(1)/D(-1) system over Q (Diophantine tuples over Q(i) with members in iQ). We construct infinitely many rational septuples of the mixed system from pairs (a,c) that are at once Pythagorean, c^2 - a^2 = +-b^2, and Eisenstein, a^2 + ac + c^2 = k^2, and determine their signs exactly: fifteen of the 21 conditions are + and six are -, the minus signs forming a K4 on four members, each forced by the arithmetic of the curve (the sign of a join is the square class of acX(P), and the base triple has sign pattern (+,-eps,eps) for every such pair). So within this construction the obstruction to an all-plus pattern is exactly six signs, and we say precisely where they are. For every such pair the triple {(a^2+c^2)/(ac), c^2/(a(a+c)), a^2/(c(a+c))} solves the mixed system; its curve is Y^2 = X(X+a^4)(X+c^4), on which S = (-a^2c^2, a^2c^2(c^2-a^2)) has order four and R = (ack^2, ack(a+c)(a^2+c^2)) infinite order, and three explicit identities give, for all but finitely many m, the septuple {rho_1,rho_2,rho_3} u {r(Q_0+2mR+jS): j=0..3}, Q_0 = R+(0,0). The pairs are the rational points of the elliptic quartic k^2 = 3m^4+n^4, infinitely many: (3,5), (-56,65), (-1425,2993), ... For (3,5) the first layer is {34/15, 25/24, 9/40, 2143479/1115560, 2059200/4669921, 2113225/1145814, -137344/15}, whose reflection in the strong member 25/24 is exactly the septuple of rStation Paper 21 read over Q: a rational septuple of the mixed system with fifteen plus and six minus signs.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: Version 2 of Paper 89, correcting the point raised in the review. (1) The false statements that the original rational problem is the all-plus case of the mixed system 1 - xy = +-square 'after x -> -x' are removed from the abstract, the introduction, Theorem 1.1(e) and Remark 4.3; the relation to the original problem is now stated only through x = ir over Q(i), and it is said explicitly that over Q the all-plus and all-minus cases are the problems xy - 1 = -square and xy - 1 = square, not the original one, since negating members does not change xy. (2) The six minus signs are presented as an obstruction within this mixed/Q(i) construction, and Remark 4.3 now states that the construction yields neither a rational Diophantine septuple nor a nonexistence proof. (3) The search code for the range 0 < a < c < 3000 is added to the supplement (search_pairs.py). (4) Display fixes: the three identities (A), (B), (C) are now separate displayed equations (the aligned block with tags did not render), and the proof labels no longer start paragraphs with '(e)'. No mathematical content is changed.

title: Rational septuples of the mixed system 1 - xy = +-square: infinitely many from Pythagorean-Eisenstein pairs, with exactly six forced minus signs
